blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.prompt: I bought a clothes rack from IKEA.
exercises.why: The direct object of a verb with negation (with не) is often in the genitive case instead of the accusative: *Я пью молоко. — Я не пью молока. Я вижу реку. — Я не вижу реки.* The verb ждать takes no preposition. The object is in the accusative case if animate and in the genitive case if inanimate: *Я жду жену. Я жду письма. The genitive case is used to denote an indefinite quantity of something: *Дайте воды, молока, хлеба.* Several masculine nouns may take the ending -у, -ю (instead of -а, -я) in the genitive case when a quantity is expressed: *Дайте, пожалуйста, супу, сахару, чаю. Хотите стакан чаю? — DLI, Lessons 23, 24, 27 and 33.  ·  «The accusative case is used to denote the direct object of the preceding verb and answers the questions кого? — whom? or что? — what?» — DLI, Lesson 18.
